title: Implement incremental KV cache compaction worker (budgeted bytes/time + safe stop conditions)
creator: Omar El-Sayed
description:
Context
- We are seeing burst-driven tail latency spikes (p95/p99) in sustained decode workloads with mixed sequence lengths due to KV arena fragmentation + opportunistic evictions at bad times.
- This ticket is the core “worker loop” that performs compaction incrementally with strict budgeting, so we can reduce fragmentation without introducing new decode stalls.

Goal
- Implement an incremental compaction worker that:
  1) moves KV pages/blocks in small steps,
  2) enforces a configurable budget (bytes moved and/or time),
  3) has safe stopping conditions to avoid correctness hazards and latency cliffs,
  4) exposes metrics and tracing hooks needed for canary + SRE guardrails.

Non-goals (in this ticket)
- UI/Console configuration (handled via flags/config only, ENG-4826).
- Final scheduler phase wiring (ENG-4824 owns the scheduling-loop integration; we just provide a worker API that can be called at safe boundaries).
- Eviction policy logic (ENG-4825). Worker should be able to request/receive an eviction decision, but not implement selection.

Proposed approach (incremental worker)
- Core concept: a compaction “step” relocates one or a small set of contiguous KV blocks from a fragmented region into a target contiguous region, updating allocator metadata atomically and preserving sequence correctness.
- The worker runs in short bursts:
  - invoked from scheduler at prefill/decode boundary OR a background maintenance thread that is gated to safe windows (final gating is ENG-4824).
  - each invocation consumes a bounded budget and then yields.

Inputs / configuration knobs (runtime flags)
- kv_compaction.enabled: bool (default false until rollout)
- kv_compaction.trigger_fragmentation_ratio: float (e.g., 0.20–0.35 depending tier; default TBD via experiments)
- kv_compaction.max_bytes_per_step: int (bytes moved cap per invocation)
- kv_compaction.max_ms_per_step: int (wall time cap per invocation)
- kv_compaction.max_steps_per_tick: int (additional guardrail to prevent long loops)
- kv_compaction.min_free_run_bytes_to_target: int (avoid churn on tiny holes)
- kv_compaction.abort_on_high_decode_pressure: bool (worker checks scheduler signals)

Worker API (internal)
- CompactionBudget { max_bytes, max_ms, max_steps }
- CompactionRequest { reason, budget, priority, allow_eviction_hint }
- CompactionResult { bytes_moved, pages_moved, steps, ms_spent, stop_reason, fragmentation_before, fragmentation_after }
- StopReason enums (examples):
  - BudgetExhaustedBytes
  - BudgetExhaustedTime
  - NoWorkFound
  - ArenaLockContention
  - DecodePressureHigh
  - EvictionRequiredButDisallowed
  - RelocationConflict (in-flight seq, pinned, etc.)
  - Cancelled / Shutdown

Safe stopping conditions (must-have)
- Hard budget caps:
  - stop immediately when bytes_moved >= max_bytes_per_step
  - stop immediately when elapsed_ms >= max_ms_per_step
  - stop when steps >= max_steps_per_tick
- Backpressure integration points:
  - if scheduler reports “decode behind” / high queue depth / tail latency risk, abort with stop_reason=DecodePressureHigh.
  - do not start a relocation if remaining budget is below the minimum copy cost for the candidate block.
- Concurrency/correctness:
  - never relocate pages for a sequence that is actively being appended to in the current decode microbatch.
  - relocation must be coordinated with cancellation: if a request is cancelled mid-relocation, worker must either complete metadata swap safely or roll back cleanly (no leaked pages, no double-free).
  - allocator locks: compaction must not hold the arena lock across long GPU copies; must support a two-phase protocol (select candidate under lock -> copy -> commit metadata under lock) or equivalent.

Relocation protocol (implementation notes)
- Candidate selection (under arena lock):
  - identify fragmented region(s) / holes and movable blocks, skipping:
    - pinned sessions
    - blocks marked “in decode” / “unsafe_to_move”
    - blocks with refcount > 1 (if applicable)
  - choose a destination run large enough to reduce fragmentation meaningfully (min_free_run_bytes_to_target).
- Copy/pack:
  - use existing copy path first (memcpy / device-to-device copy) and only add microkernel if profiling shows it’s needed.
  - copy should be cancellable at the worker level (i.e., we can stop before starting a new block); do not attempt mid-kernel cancellation.
- Commit:
  - update block table / page map with a commit marker that is crash-safe for the process lifetime (we don’t persist, but we need consistency under concurrent readers).
  - release source pages back to free list after commit.

Metrics / tracing (minimal to unblock canary)
- Counters:
  - kv_compaction_bytes_moved_total
  - kv_compaction_pages_moved_total
  - kv_compaction_steps_total
  - kv_compaction_abort_total{reason=...}
- Histograms:
  - kv_compaction_step_ms
  - kv_compaction_bytes_per_step
- Gauges:
  - kv_fragmentation_ratio (from ENG-4822; worker should log before/after and expose in result)
- Tracing:
  - span per invocation with stop_reason, bytes moved, fragmentation_before/after, and whether eviction was requested.

Perf acceptance criteria (must meet before enabling beyond internal canary)
- No more than +0.5% regression in steady-state throughput on decode-heavy benchmarks when compaction is enabled but not actively triggered.
- When compaction is triggered under the benchmark plan “mixed length bursts”, compaction overhead should not add >2ms to median decode step on A100/H100 (measured at scheduler boundary), and should reduce fragmentation ratio by >= 10% relative within 5 minutes of sustained load (exact target to be validated with experiments tracker).
- p99 latency in perf-canary scenario must not regress by >3% versus baseline with compaction enabled at default budgets; if it regresses, stop_reason and traces must make the cause diagnosable (e.g., excessive bytes per step, lock contention).

Test plan
- Unit tests:
  - relocation bookkeeping (no double-free, no leaks)
  - stop condition enforcement (bytes/time/steps)
  - “no work found” behavior when arena is already contiguous
- Integration/stress tests (ENG-4827 will add broader coverage; include a minimal version here):
  - long-lived sessions + churn + cancellations
  - repeated compaction invocations do not cause fragmentation oscillation (thrash)
- Benchmark validation:
  - run benchmark plan scenarios with compaction off/on at varying budgets; capture bytes moved, abort reasons, and p95/p99.

Rollout notes
- Must be behind feature flag (ENG-4826 config plumbing).
- Default to disabled in all tiers until perf canary passes and SRE guardrails are approved.

Open questions
- Budget enforcement priority: prefer bytes cap, time cap, or both? (ADR says both are supported; we need a clear “which one ends the step first” semantics.)
- Candidate selection heuristic: best-first by “largest hole elimination” vs “largest movable block” vs “most fragmented segment”. Start simple and iterate based on experiments.
- Interaction with eviction: should the worker ever request eviction proactively when it can’t find a destination run, or leave to scheduler/eviction ticket? Proposal: worker returns stop_reason=EvictionRequiredButDisallowed with a hint and lets ENG-4825 integrate policy.

Owner notes
- Samir: implement worker loop + stop conditions + two-phase relocation protocol.
- Sofia (ENG-4824): call points / gating in scheduler; will likely consume CompactionResult for logging + guardrails.
- Allison/Sean: confirm metrics naming aligns with metrics standard once ENG-4822 lands.
acceptance_criteria: Compaction worker exposes a single entry point that executes <= budget (bytes/ms/steps) and returns a structured stop_reason.
Relocation protocol does not hold arena lock across GPU copy; no allocator corruption under concurrency (stress test: cancellations + churn).
Worker can be invoked repeatedly without increasing fragmentation (no thrash) when trigger conditions are not met.
Tracing/metrics emitted per invocation are sufficient to correlate compaction activity to tail latency spikes in canary (bytes moved, ms spent, stop_reason, frag before/after).
Perf: throughput regression <= 0.5% in steady decode when enabled but idle; and no >3% p99 regression in perf-canary at default budgets.
